papers.title_en: Trust Your Instincts: Confidence-Driven Test-Time RL for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Siyao Chen, Jiakang Yuan, Jiaxin Wang, Tao Chen
papers.evidence: 将轨迹级相似性作为长时程任务的奖励信号
papers.tldr: 现有视觉-语言-动作模型(VLA)的强化学习依赖外部环境反馈，限制了自主改进。我们利用VLA内部评估能力，提出基于轨迹置信度的内在奖励机制，无需外部奖励信号。通过信心驱动的双专家引导，T^2VLA在LIBERO和RoboTwin上超越监督基线，接近真实奖励的oracle RL性能。该框架适用于多种VLA架构，实现了无需外界交互的自我提升。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become indispensable for pushing Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) beyond static imitation learning. However, existing RL methods typically require external environmental feedback, relying on predefined success signals to guide policy updates. In this work, we show that VLA models possess useful internal evaluative capabilities: in discrete-action VLAs, trajectories with higher generation confidence are significantly more likely to succeed. Based on this observation, we introduce T^2VLA (Test-time VLA), an architecture-agnostic test-time RL framework that enables VLA models to achieve self-bootstrapping policy improvement. Instead of relying on external rewards, T^2VLA leverages trajectory-level similarity to high-confidence expert demonstrations as an intrinsic reward signal. In addition, we propose a Confidence-Driven Dual Expert Bootstrapping mechanism, which dynamically balances a Local Pseudo-Expert for exploration and a Global Expert Pool for training stability. Extensive experiments on the LIBERO and RoboTwin benchmarks show that T^2VLA consistently outperforms supervised baselines and approaches oracle RL performance with ground-truth rewards, achieving effective improvement without external reward feedback. Furthermore, T^2VLA adapts to distinct VLA paradigms, including both OpenVLA-OFT and the pi series.

papers.title_en: Rank-Then-Act: Reward-Free Control from Frame-Order Progress
papers.authors: Yuriy Maksyuta, George Bredis, Ruslan Rakhimov, Daniil Gavrilov
papers.evidence: 通过基于VLM的帧序进展排序和相关性奖励，无需显式奖励即可学习控制策略，实现长期奖励分配
papers.tldr: 针对从演示视频中学习控制策略时缺乏环境奖励的问题，提出Rank-Then-Act框架，通过训练视觉语言模型预测帧序进度，并基于排序相关性生成奖励信号，实现无奖励强化学习。该方法利用专家视频中的时序信息自动构建密集奖励，避免了手工设计。实验表明，在长期控制任务中，RTA优于此前的无奖励方法，甚至接近有监督上限。该技术可应用于无人机输电线路巡检等需要长时间连续视觉观察的任务，提供自动化的奖励分配机制。
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Rank-Then-Act (RTA), a framework for learning control policies from expert video demonstrations without environment rewards. RTA trains a Vision-Language Model (VLM) offline as a progress-based ordinal scorer, using a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) objective over shuffled frame sequences, which forces the model to recover temporal ordering from visual semantics rather than trivial time cues. Importantly, instead of using the scorer directly as a scalar reward model, we propose a correlation-based reward function for reinforcement learning: at each interaction window, we compute the Spearman rank correlation between predicted progress rankings and true temporal indices, yielding a bounded, scale-invariant learning signal. This design decouples reward learning from absolute calibration and enables stable transfer across tasks and environments. We evaluate RTA on discrete control benchmarks (PyBoy: Catrap, Kirby) and continuous control tasks (PointMaze, MetaWorld). RTA consistently matches or outperforms prior video-based reward learning methods and rank-based baselines, while demonstrating strong cross-task reuse of a single pretrained progress scorer. Our results suggest that correlation-structured supervision over video-derived ordinal signals is sufficient for policy learning, offering a scalable alternative to explicit reward design.
